master.master_headline: Holding at 8: Shenzhen brought a nuclear-talks pledge with no dates, and the Gulf is still tense.
master.master_reasoning: This is judgment, not measurement. Same method as before: anchor on the closest civilisation-scale threats, nuclear (4.5) and great-power war (6.5), set the master farther out because those desks' midnights are lower bars than a civilisation-wide point of no return, then pull it back in because one conflict drives several threats at once and correlated risks compound. The main event since last edition has now been reported. At the Shenzhen meeting the three leaders said nuclear war must never be fought and promised a nuclear-risk dialogue, but set no date, venue or treaty and made no Iran or Ukraine deal. That lowers the temperature of the talk, not the risk itself. Against it, Iran warned it might strike first as another US carrier arrived (seen as a headline only). All sixteen desks held their figures. I make one small move: the economy comes in slightly because the fact-checker now confirms the stress figures I could not confirm last time (a fifth straight stock loss, the 10-year yield near 5.07%, Fed minutes leaning toward more hikes). Lower oil and no credit failure hold that move to a small step. Resources holds: S&P's count shows Hormuz crossings flat in October, which does not fit neatly with the 65% shortfall figure, and the desk flags the two as unreconciled. The board's net movement is close to zero, so the master holds at 8 with a steady trend.

most_pressing.why: There is no licensed vaccine for this strain and funding is slow, though weekly growth is steady and exports are contained.

master.where_headed: Next: the COP31 close on 20 Nov, any IAEA board outcome, and whether the Shenzhen dialogue pledge gets a date and a venue. After that: Israel's coalition deadline on 6 Dec (extendable), the Fed meeting on 8-9 Dec with a hike expected and its size debated, US inflation data on 10 Dec, and the EU ministers' meeting on 14 Dec where sanctions over the fridge attacks are expected. Over two years the main risks are unchanged: no arms-control successor, AI capability and money running ahead of oversight, and a strong El Nino meeting 2027 harvests while Gulf shipping and fertiliser stay tight. Fixes keep advancing but will arrive too late for this window.

master.dissent: A reader could argue for 7.5: the summit produced words, not limits; Iran is threatening to strike first; markets have fallen five days in a row with yields above 5%; and Ebola is mostly untraced. The case for 8.5 is also there: the three nuclear powers are talking for the first time, oil is falling, credit is calm, no desk moved on its own evidence, and Hormuz crossings by one count are not getting worse.

Gulf tension stayed high: Iran warned it might strike first as another US carrier arrived (headline-level reports only).
Markets slid further: the S&P 500 posted a fifth straight loss, the 10-year yield sat near 5.07%, and Fed minutes leaned toward more hikes; the economy clock moved slightly closer (8.5 to 8.3).

Eased or flat: oil fell about 3% to near $83, S&P counts October Hormuz crossings level with September, Kenya and Nigeria saw no onward Ebola spread, and no new cyber incident appeared.
Still pending: the IAEA board outcome and the COP31 close (due 20 Nov).

desks.name: AI Frontier & Safety
desks.midnight_definition: AI systems that can do essentially all cognitive work better, faster and cheaper than humans arrive before society has put effective steering or oversight in place (frontier threshold is the one that matters most).
desks.headline: Anthropic ANT closes day one at $97.17; California suit against OpenAI reported
desks.summary: Anthropic's Nasdaq debut on 19 Nov raised $81.34B at $83 and closed at $97.17, 17.1% above the IPO price. Separately, a roundup reports California sued OpenAI over agent safeguards, Google flagged the first autonomous AI attack seen in the wild, and Commerce issued an interim rule on remote access to AI chips. Oversight is arriving as litigation and export rules, not as capability limits.

desks.name: Biosecurity & Pandemics
desks.midnight_definition: A pandemic or biological event worse than COVID-19 in global deaths and disruption.
desks.headline: Ebola tops 11,200 cases, 80% untraced; US loses measles elimination status
desks.summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DRC is the second-largest on record: UKHSA reports 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths as of 9 Nov (+510 in a week), and government data cited on 15-17 Nov show over 11,200 cases and 5,500 deaths. Africa CDC says over 80% of new cases are outside contact lists; of $2.9bn pledged, $1.3bn has been released. PAHO formally revoked US measles elimination on 17 Nov (over 5,400 US cases in 2026); the pandemic-agreement pathogen annex is still pending, due no later than May 2027.

top_stories.why_it_matters: Over 11,200 cases and 5,500 deaths in 8 of 26 provinces; over 80% of new cases untraced, over 65% of deaths in the community; $1.3bn of $2.9bn pledged released; two vaccine trials approved, results expected early 2027.

top_stories.why_it_matters: PAHO found measles circulated uninterrupted for over a year; the US has logged over 5,400 cases in 2026, weakening a regional vaccination benchmark.

trajectory.two_years: Outcome hinges on whether the PABS annex is agreed and surveillance and vaccination capacity recover. A COVID-scale event remains a tail risk rather than a baseline.

desks.name: Biotech, Longevity & BCI
desks.midnight_definition: The first therapy shown in humans to slow or reverse biological ageing broadly, not just one disease.
desks.headline: Moderna and Merck still 'working toward' melanoma vaccine filing; no ageing endpoint yet
desks.summary: Moderna's Q3 report (6 Nov 2026) says it and Merck are working toward regulatory submissions for the personalised melanoma vaccine, with no filing date given. The Yale-led Nature Medicine review shows epigenetic-age markers move with some interventions but not that lives get longer or healthier. Narrow-disease progress continues; no human clinical ageing endpoint has appeared.

top_stories.title: Moderna Q3: melanoma vaccine still 'working toward' regulatory submissions
top_stories.why_it_matters: Shows no confirmed filing yet, only preparation for launch subject to approval; also notes FDA approved Moderna's seasonal flu vaccine in Aug 2026 and a norovirus Phase 3 interim missed early-success criteria.

top_stories.title: Yale-led review of 51 trials: which interventions shift epigenetic age
top_stories.why_it_matters: Largest human check of ageing-clock responsiveness: exercise plus diet, metformin, semaglutide and anti-TNF drugs moved the markers, supplements did not. The outcome was a biomarker, not lifespan or disease, so it does not meet the midnight threshold.

Resolves last edition's date discrepancy in favour of 19 Aug, per trade press dated that day.

trajectory.two_years: Personalised vaccines and in vivo editing plausibly approved; ageing trials will probably still report biomarkers or single-disease endpoints until a validated clinical ageing endpoint is accepted.

desks.name: Semiconductors & Quantum
desks.midnight_definition: A fault-tolerant quantum computer performs commercially or cryptographically relevant work (e.g. breaking RSA/elliptic-curve keys) that classical machines cannot.
desks.headline: Nvidia's record $115.8B quarter confirmed; Quantinuum cuts logical error rate 10x
desks.summary: Nvidia's own release confirms record Q3 revenue of $115.8B and a $130B Q4 guide that assumes no China data-centre compute sales; the CEO search continues with CFO Kress interim. In quantum, Quantinuum reported a roughly 10x lower logical error rate on Helios (company claim, 19 Oct), consistent with steady incremental progress but no independent fault-tolerance proof.

desks.name: Climate & Earth Systems
desks.midnight_definition: Crossing self-reinforcing tipping points (ice sheets, AMOC, Amazon, coral reefs, permafrost) that lock in severe warming regardless of later action.
desks.headline: COP31 due to close 20 Nov with no final text yet indexed; El Nino near-historic
desks.summary: COP31 in Antalya is scheduled to close 20 Nov, working from Australia's 16 Nov cover-decision draft (fossil-fuel exit wording, a 35% electrification goal by 2035, USD 120bn adaptation finance, 1.5C overshoot concern, net zero by 2030 for rich countries); Bowen says the final will be narrowed. No coverage after 17 Nov could be found, so the outcome is unknown. NOAA's 12 Nov update (+2.5C Nino 3.4, about 60% odds of a historic event) is the latest ENSO reading; no new tipping-element science verified.

top_stories.title: EU warns COP31 draft could make talks untenable; another draft expected
top_stories.why_it_matters: Consensus rules let one party block; the draft asks for fossil phase-out and net zero for rich countries by 2030, and an IPCC AR7 timing dispute is also live. Overrun past 20 Nov is plausible.

top_stories.title: COP31 day-by-day: red lines on methane, electrification, adaptation finance
top_stories.why_it_matters: LMDCs object to methane being singled out; Arab Group and Russia oppose the 35% electrification goal; tripling adaptation finance (about 120bn USD figure) is pushed into finance talks by the EU, Japan and others.

top_stories.title: Australia's 16 Nov draft: faster fossil exit, 35% electrification, 120bn adaptation
top_stories.why_it_matters: Sets the text the final deal will be cut from; Bowen says it will be narrowed and observers expect fierce resistance on fossil wording, amid energy-crisis tensions.

top_stories.title: Draft carries two fossil wordings; Bowen says final will differ
top_stories.why_it_matters: One option repeats 2023 'transitioning away' wording and a stronger one says 'phase out'; either may be dropped.

top_stories.title: NOAA: El Nino strengthening, about 60% chance of historic strength
top_stories.why_it_matters: Over 79% odds of strong-to-very-strong through Jan-Mar 2027 raises odds of record 2027 heat, coral and weather stress.

top_stories.title: Pledged public climate finance from big donors about 70% below 2025
top_stories.why_it_matters: Aid cuts shrink adaptation money as disputes over developed-country obligations deepen.

trajectory.six_months: COP31 probably closes with a compromise cover decision, possibly after overrunning; El Nino peaks around the turn of the year and monthly temperature records are likely into early 2027.
trajectory.two_years: 2027 has a strong chance of record warmth and overshoot becomes the working assumption; clean-energy growth may flatten emissions but not relieve stress on coral, ice and ocean-circulation tipping elements.

signals_to_watch: Next COP31 draft and final cover decision (20 Nov, overrun possible): does fossil phase-out or transition wording survive?
Fate of 35% electrification goal, 1.5C overshoot language and adaptation finance tripling
IPCC AR7 timing dispute; IPCC session in December
NOAA ENSO update 10 Dec; Copernicus bulletin early Dec

desks.name: Cyber & Critical Infrastructure

desks.headline: France expects EU Iran sanctions on 14 Dec over fridge attacks; no new escalation
desks.summary: No new major incident surfaced since the 6 am edition. France's foreign minister said on 16 Nov he is confident EU foreign ministers will agree sanctions on those responsible for the October fridge campaign at their 14 Dec meeting, with a large majority of states behind him. France blames Iran's IRGC; Tehran calls the accusation baseless. The US joint advisory (5 Nov) and EU warning (4 Nov) confirm a cross-border threat; effects remain local and recover in days.

top_stories.title: France expects EU sanctions on Iran over fridge hack at 14 Dec ministers' meeting
top_stories.why_it_matters: Gives the sanctions track a concrete date; France says most member states back it. Hundreds of French supermarkets were hit on 11-12 Oct and incidents occurred in at least 11 other European countries in early November.

top_stories.title: France to seek EU sanctions on Iran over fridge cyberattacks; 15 fires
top_stories.why_it_matters: A cyber campaign with physical effects is becoming a formal EU sanctions matter. Iran's UN mission did not respond in the coverage seen; Tehran routinely denies such operations.

top_stories.title: FBI, CISA and three agencies warn of attacks on refrigeration controllers
top_stories.why_it_matters: The US government says attackers are exploiting internet-exposed temperature controllers worldwide to force heating or defrost cycles. Sectors at risk include grocery, healthcare, chemicals and transport; the advisory names no actor.

top_stories.title: US warns on refrigeration hacks amid suspected military commissary attacks
top_stories.why_it_matters: Joint US agencies urge taking controllers offline; officials suspect Iran-linked disruption at about six military commissaries since late August. The US notice names no actor; the Iran comparison is an outside expert's view.

top_stories.title: CISA and partners extend Iran PLC advisory to Schneider and Siemens devices
top_stories.why_it_matters: Iranian-affiliated actors first hit Rockwell PLCs in April; the update widens targeting to other vendors. Corrects last edition's approximate November date.

top_stories.title: UK cyber resilience bill: Lords defeat government twice before Commons return
top_stories.why_it_matters: Lords voted for a statutory review within 12 months and a register of hostile cyber powers; the Commons must now decide on these changes.

trajectory.six_months: Expect an EU sanctions listing on Iranian IRGC-linked persons, more exploitation of exposed cold-chain and PLC devices, and copycat or retaliatory activity. Most incidents stay local and last days.
trajectory.two_years: A large pool of poorly secured operational technology, AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and normalised state retaliation raise the odds of a multi-sector event, though hardening mandates (US advisories, UK bill) could blunt it.

desks.headline: S&P 500 hits 5th straight loss; minutes back more hikes, Waller floats 50bp
desks.summary: US stocks slipped again on 18 Nov (S&P 500 7,323.63, -0.23%, fifth straight loss; Dow -1.11%; Nasdaq +0.42%) after October FOMC minutes showed nearly all officials expect further hikes. Governor Waller said a half-point December move may be needed, yet prediction markets still leaned heavily to 25bp. Long yields eased slightly from 5.1% highs, oil fell, the dollar hit a 19-month-plus high, and the VIX stood at 24.5; no bank or credit failure surfaced.

desks.headline: FERC stalled PJM's 6.8 GW backstop; fusion still pre-net-energy
desks.summary: FERC only partly approved PJM's one-time reliability backstop on 29 Sep, found cost-allocation and collateral terms possibly unjust, and PJM pulled its 30 Sep auction with no new schedule as of the latest report seen. On fusion, SPARC and Helion are both still pre-net-energy; Helion ran deuterium-tritium fuel at 150 million C in early 2026 and still targets 2028, while CFS targets 2027 for switching on SPARC.

desks.headline: Xi, Trump, Putin pledge nuclear-risk dialogue, but no deadline, treaty or Iran/Ukraine deal
desks.summary: The first three-way Xi-Trump-Putin meeting took place in Shenzhen on 19 November (about 70 minutes) and produced a joint declaration that nuclear war must never be fought and a pledge to start a dialogue on nuclear risk, with no timetable, format or treaty. No breakthrough was announced on Iran or Ukraine. In the Gulf, Iran warned on 16 November it might strike first before another US attack as a US carrier arrived, and the Hormuz disruption and the reported US blockade persist (not re-verified this edition).

top_stories.title: Trump, Xi, Putin pledge nuclear dialogue after Shenzhen summit
top_stories.why_it_matters: A joint declaration says nuclear war has no winners and commits to talks on reducing nuclear risk, but gives no deadline, format or treaty; New START lapsed in February with no successor. Also agreed in outline: UN reform and more refined-fuel supply; no Iran or Ukraine breakthrough.

desks.name: Nuclear & Strategic Weapons
desks.midnight_definition: The first use of a nuclear weapon in war, or an uncontrolled escalation toward large-scale nuclear exchange, which cannot be undone.
desks.headline: Iran bars enriched uranium leaving country; IAEA board outcome still unreported
desks.summary: No treaty has capped US and Russian strategic arsenals since New START lapsed in February 2026, and the Bulletin's Doomsday Clock stands at a record 85 seconds. The IAEA board already found Iran in noncompliance and referred it to the UN Security Council on 9 September (23-3), where Russian and Chinese vetoes make action unlikely; inspectors have not located Iran's roughly 440 kg of near-weapons-grade uranium, and Iranian clerics are debating dropping the no-bomb pledge. North Korea is expanding enrichment and Russia-NATO nuclear signalling continues at a steady level.

trajectory.two_years: Without a successor framework, warhead uploads and a three-way US-Russia-China build-up become the default. Iran's nuclear choice and the testing moratorium are the main wildcards.

desks.name: Food, Water & Resources
desks.midnight_definition: Simultaneous failure of several major food-producing regions, or a resource shock, that causes mass hunger across multiple continents.
desks.headline: NOAA confirms El Niño near +2.5C with record odds; Egypt fertiliser gas cuts persist
desks.summary: NOAA's 12 Nov update (via a local-news report) puts the Nino-3.4 anomaly near +2.5C, with over 79% odds of a strong-to-very-strong event through Jan-Mar 2027 and about 60% odds of a record. Egypt's fertiliser gas cuts of 20-33% have no end date and urea is near $535/t. Hormuz crossings recovered to a three-month high in October (S&P) while attacks continue, and Sudan, South Sudan, Yemen and Gaza stay the top hunger hotspots; headline food prices remain moderate.

top_stories.title: NOAA 12 Nov: El Niño near +2.5C, over 79% odds strong into early 2027
top_stories.why_it_matters: A strong event is expected to keep building into winter and weaken in early 2027, with about 60% odds of record strength. This raises 2027 yield risk in Southern Hemisphere and Asian crop regions; next update is 10 Dec.

top_stories.title: Egypt fertiliser gas cut reaches 33% at Mopco; plant reports conflict
top_stories.why_it_matters: The 33% cut took effect 8 Nov after 20% from 1 Nov, with no end date. Abu Qir is reported at 33% by one outlet and 20% by another, and Kima has only confirmed 20%. Granular urea is about $535/t FOB.

top_stories.title: Hormuz crossings at 750 in October, a three-month high, despite attacks
top_stories.why_it_matters: S&P counted 750 transits (749 in September), with LNG carriers at 32, the most since the conflict began, but crude VLCCs fell to 156 from 184. Red Sea Bab al-Mandab transits rose to 1,196. This is a different measure from UKMTO's 65% below pre-war figure last edition.

top_stories.title: UKMTO: Hormuz transits about 65% below pre-war, 11 ships hit in a week
top_stories.why_it_matters: UKMTO counted 170 outbound and 155 inbound transits and JMIC held the threat at severe. Oil, LNG and fertiliser freight stay exposed.

top_stories.title: FAO-WFP Hunger Hotspots: 13 hotspots, 266 million in acute food insecurity
top_stories.why_it_matters: Sudan, South Sudan, Yemen and Gaza top the list, with Northeast Nigeria and Somalia added. Sudan faces famine risk in 14 areas and projected IPC 5 cases of 200,000; food aid funding fell about 59% from 2022 to 2025. This outlook runs to November 2026 and is dated.

trajectory.six_months: Fertiliser costs and a peaking-then-fading very strong El Niño shape 2027 planting and early harvests; Sudan and other hotspots stay at famine risk without more aid.
trajectory.two_years: If Hormuz stays impaired and a record El Niño cuts yields in several regions, a multi-continent food price spike is plausible; if shipping normalises the system probably absorbs it with rising regional hunger.

desks.summary: Narrow autonomy keeps scaling: Baidu's Apollo Go reached 30 cities by October and Tesla opened unsupervised robotaxis in San Antonio on 9 Nov, but independent trackers showed only tens of unsupervised Tesla cars in April and Musk deferred large scale to a software overhaul due late 2026 to early 2027. Tesla's Q3 update floated 20,000 Optimus robots a week by 2027 while admitting the robot struggles with varied tasks, so humanoid claims remain far ahead of delivered work.

desks.name: Global Health & Demographics
desks.midnight_definition: Demographic and social strain (ageing, shrinking workforces, health-funding collapse) becomes so severe that major societies can no longer sustain their pensions, health systems and workforce.
desks.headline: Global health aid to hit $42.6B in 2026, lowest since 2012; US measles at 5,412
desks.summary: IHME estimates development assistance for health falls to $42.6 billion in 2026, down 5% on 2025 after a 12% drop in 2024, with US cuts of 45% since 2024. US measles reached 5,412 cases (CDC data to 12 Nov), up 230 in a week, with six CDC-listed deaths. Against this, WHO says global life expectancy has nearly recovered to its pre-pandemic level (73.3 vs 73.4 years).

top_stories.title: Global health aid set to fall to $42.6B in 2026, lowest since 2012
top_stories.why_it_matters: IHME estimates a 5% fall after 12% in 2024; US health aid is down about $5.9B (45%) since 2024, the UK 37%. Deepens the financing squeeze on HIV, TB and immunisation in poorer countries.

top_stories.title: US measles rises to 5,412 cases, up 230 in a week
top_stories.why_it_matters: CDC data as of 12 Nov: 43 outbreaks, 6 deaths listed, 47 jurisdictions; about 96% of cases are outbreak-linked. Shows continued spread amid weakened vaccination coverage.

top_stories.title: WHO: life expectancy 73.3 years, nearly back to pre-pandemic
top_stories.why_it_matters: Healthy life expectancy (62.8) is still 0.4 years below 2019; noncommunicable diseases cause 74% of deaths and dementia is now the fifth leading cause, which raises long-term care and pension burdens.

top_stories.why_it_matters: Donor HIV money dropped from $8.8B to $7.3B; about 1.2 million new infections and 570,000 AIDS deaths in 2025, with infections rising in 21 countries. Without faster action UNAIDS projects over 3 million extra infections by 2030.

top_stories.why_it_matters: WHO/UNICEF estimates show a slight improvement over 2024 but 74 countries are worse than in 2019. Measles coverage has not recovered, with 1.8 million more unprotected children than in 2019.

top_stories.why_it_matters: About 23,700 births in August; January-August up 14.5%. Still far below replacement, but decline is not uniform.

trajectory.two_years: Further donor retrenchment would likely reverse immunisation and HIV gains in fragile settings, while ageing keeps forcing pension fights in Europe and Asia.

desks.headline: Banda Sea M6.6-6.8 deep quake, no tsunami; Kilauea and sun stay regional
desks.summary: Hazards remain regional. The 16 Nov Banda Sea quake was rated 6.8 by Indonesia's BMKG (revised down from 7.1) and 6.6 in USGS-based listings; it was deep enough that BMKG saw no tsunami potential, and no damage was reported in early coverage. Kilauea's episode 56 (5 Nov) is the latest confirmed; I found no report that episode 57 has begun. The newest official solar report I could read (16 Nov) shows low flare odds and at most minor storms.
